newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Gadek falls on yen exposure worries.
newsitem.headline: Gadek falls on yen exposure worries.

text.p: Malaysian automotive, finance and construction company, Gadek Malaysia Bhd shed more than six percent on Tuesday on worries its subsidiaries may be affected by the Japanese yen's recent strength, analysts said.
At 0730 GMT, the stock had slid one ringgit or 6.90 percent to 13.50 ringgit, hitting an intraday low for 1997 on volume of 365,000. It fell as low as 13.10.
"There has been strong selling (of Gadek) by funds, local and foreign, due to the yen appreciating over the last six days," said Victor Wan, senior analyst at South Johor Securities.
Gadek officials could not be reached for immediate comment.
Gadek has a 32 percent stake in Hicom Holdings Bhd, which in turn controls national car maker Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd and car distributor Edaran Otomobil Nasional Bhd.

A large proportion of the local car's components are sourced from Japan and Proton has a commensurately large exposure to the currency. The yen has appreciated around six percent against the ringgit over the last week.
Gadek also assembles and distributes Mitsubishi and Isuzu four-wheel-drive vehicles imported from Japan.
Motor stocks were hit on Monday on concerns over the yen's rise, with Gadek falling 30 cents.
